name: Christies Beach Oval (Bice Oval)
address: Dyke Road & Bice Oval, Christies Beach SA 5165
title: Junior Footy Roots of Craig McRae
description: The junior grassroots proving ground where 3-time Brisbane Lions premiership player and Collingwood premiership coach Craig 'Fly' McRae first learned the craft before joining South Adelaide. Also nurtured Crows inaugural defender Nigel Smart and numerous southern suburbs stalwarts.

name: Eden Valley Oval (Barossa & Light)
title: Simon Goodwin & Barossa Country Roots
description: Heartland of the Goodwin family football lineage. Melbourne premiership coach and Adelaide Crows dual-premiership hero Simon Goodwin traces proud country roots through the Barossa and Eden Valley region, where local clubrooms preserve generations of country footy grit.

name: Alberton Oval
address: Brougham Place & Queen Street, Alberton SA 5014
title: Port Adelaide's Spiritual Home Since 1880
description: Port Adelaide's beating heart for over 145 years. Features the bronze statue of patriarch Fos Williams, the Robert B. Quinn Grandstand, Allan Scott Headquarters, and the Port Adelaide Football Club Museum holding 36 SANFL flags and the 2004 AFL premiership cup.

name: Unley Oval
address: Trimmer Terrace & Oxford Terrace, Unley SA 5061
title: Sturt Double Blues & Jack Oatey Legacy
description: The cathedral of the Sturt Football Club. Immortal coach Jack Oatey revolutionized Australian rules football here during the 1960s with team-first handball chains and precision checkside kicking, leading Sturt to 5 straight flags (1966–1970).

name: Prospect Oval
title: Home of the Roosters & Barrie Robran
description: Home ground of North Adelaide since 1922. Sacred turf where Barrie Robran (triple Magarey Medalist and AFL Hall of Fame Legend) played his career, and Ken Farmer kicked a world-record 1,472 career goals.

name: Glenelg Oval (ACH Group Stadium)
address: Brighton Road & Rugless Terrace, Glenelg SA 5045
title: The Bay Sheiks & Peter Carey Fortress
description: The seaside fortress of the Glenelg Tigers since 1921. Celebrated for Peter Carey's record 448 senior games, Graham Cornes' iconic high-flying marks, and the deafening roar of the Brighton Road outer hill.

name: Norwood Oval (Coopers Stadium)
category: Historic Club Spiritual Home & Gather Round Venue
address: The Parade & Woods Street, Norwood SA 5067
title: Redlegs Historic Home Since 1901
description: Heart of The Parade and 31-time SANFL premier Norwood FC. Renowned for its intimate red-brick grandstands, Michael Taylor Stand, and electric Gather Round suburban match-day atmosphere.

name: Richmond Oval (Hisense Stadium)
title: West Adelaide & Neil Kerley's 'Blood 'n' Tars'
description: Home ground of West Adelaide since 1958. Immortalized by Neil Kerley's fiery leadership, Tony Modra's breathtaking early screamers, and the 2008 Brownlow Medalist Adam Cooney's junior days.

name: Elizabeth Oval (X Convenience Oval)
title: Central District Bulldogs Dynasty Fortress
description: Fortress of the Central District Bulldogs in Adelaide's northern manufacturing heartland. Site of the modern era's most dominant dynasty: 9 SANFL flags in 11 years (2000–2010), home of John Platten and the Gowans twins.
